data.description:
## The question

Commit `9c7d78127696` ("Revert scanner-integration Verified gate") reverted `6125c5345f01` ("Pin
review scanner contracts in Verified") **wholesale**, for reasons unrelated to most of what that
commit contained: a vacuous `Verified` vote and a red required job blocking every open change.

`6125c5345f01` touched **12 files**, including `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` and four test
files. **One casualty is already confirmed:** it had added marker-honouring assertions to
`tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py`, and the revert removed them, silently breaking the
`# mechanism-ok:` contributor path (`satin-fullgrown-shibainu`, `affd-913c-3fb0-40fb`).

Nobody noticed for weeks, because the assertions were the only expression of that contract and
their removal broke nothing that was being watched.

**The question this ticket asks: what ELSE did that revert drop?**

## Why this deserves its own investigation rather than an assumption

The reverting commit's stated purpose was narrow — stop a bad gate from blocking changes. Reverting
it wholesale was a reasonable emergency move. But a wholesale revert of a 12-file commit removes
everything that commit added, including work that had nothing to do with the problem being solved.

The ratchet contract was found only because a contributor hit the wall months later and an
investigation traced it back. That is not a detection mechanism; it is luck. Any other cross-cutting
contract introduced by `6125c5345f01` is in the same position right now: gone, unwatched, and
undetectable until someone trips over it.

I am explicitly NOT assuming there are others. There may be none — the other 11 files may have been
purely scanner-gate machinery that was correctly removed with the gate. That is a valid outcome and
should be recorded as such.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enumerate every file and hunk `6125c5345f01` added, and for each, state whether
      `9c7d78127696` removing it was INTENDED (scanner-gate machinery) or COLLATERAL (a contract or
      capability unrelated to the gate).
- [ ] For each collateral item, decide and record: re-apply, or deliberately leave removed with a
      reason. Do not re-apply by default — some of it may genuinely belong with the reverted gate.
- [ ] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` and the four test files are examined specifically, since
      generated-artifact and test-shaped changes are the most likely to carry a contract whose loss
      is silent.
- [ ] The general lesson is recorded somewhere durable: a cross-cutting contract expressed ONLY
      inside a feature commit has no independent existence and will not survive that commit being
      reverted. Whether that becomes guidance, a check, or nothing is a judgement call — but make it
      deliberately rather than letting the observation evaporate with this ticket.
- [ ] If the audit finds nothing else, say so plainly and close it as `not_a_bug` with the
      enumeration attached. A clean audit is a useful result and stops the next person re-running it.
data.title: Audit what else the wholesale scanner-gate revert dropped: it reverted a 12-file commit for one narrow reason, and one confirmed casualty (the mechanism-ok contract) went unnoticed for weeks
